sinks.name: TA_InvokeCommandEntryPoint

sinks.reason: Selects which command handler runs, affecting control flow and security-sensitive operations performed on provided parameters

sinks.reason: Describes how to interpret the parameters array, enabling parsing/validation of input/output data

sinks.reason: controls how the session is established and may influence authorization or parameter interpretation

sinks.name: TA_OpenSessionEntryPoint
sinks.reason: contains client-supplied data that may be parsed/validated/transformed to initialize session state

sinks.name: TA_OpenSessionEntryPoint
sinks.reason: stores TA-defined per-session state derived from or influenced by client inputs

sinks.name: TEE_AllocateTransientObject
sinks.reason: Determines what kind of cryptographic/key object is allocated, influencing how sensitive material may be stored/handled.

sinks.name: TEE_AllocateTransientObject
sinks.reason: Controls size of the transient object (often key size); affects security properties and allocation for sensitive data.

sinks.role: out handle to allocated transient object

sinks.reason: reads message bytes to be hashed/finalized

sinks.reason: controls how much input data is read from the buffer

sinks.reason: writes computed digest result to caller-provided memory

sinks.name: TEE_DigestUpdate
sinks.reason: Identifies the ongoing hash/digest context that will be updated with provided data, affecting cryptographic state.

sinks.reason: Points to message bytes that are read and incorporated into the digest computation.

sinks.name: TEE_DigestUpdate

sinks.name: TEE_GetObjectBufferAttribute

sinks.name: TEE_GetObjectBufferAttribute
sinks.reason: controls which attribute (potentially key material or other sensitive buffer attribute) is retrieved

sinks.name: TEE_GetObjectBufferAttribute
sinks.reason: receives copied attribute data, which may be sensitive

sinks.name: TEE_GetObjectBufferAttribute
sinks.reason: governs how much sensitive data is written and exposes length information

sinks.name: TEE_InitRefAttribute
sinks.reason: receives and stores a reference to caller-provided data pointer/length, affecting how later cryptographic operations interpret input

sinks.name: TEE_InitRefAttribute
sinks.reason: controls how much data is referenced/used; impacts bounds and correctness of subsequent use

sinks.reason: Message data is read to finalize MAC computation

sinks.name: TEE_MACCompareFinal
sinks.reason: Controls how many bytes are read from the message buffer

sinks.reason: Tag value is read and compared against computed MAC (security-sensitive comparison)

sinks.name: TEE_MACCompareFinal

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Holds cryptographic state and key material used to compute the final MAC

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Message bytes are read to compute/update the MAC

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Controls how many bytes are read from the input buffer

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Receives the computed MAC tag (security-sensitive output)

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Determines output size and may be updated with actual tag length, affecting how much is written

sinks.name: TEE_MACInit

sinks.name: TEE_MACInit
sinks.reason: Reads IV/nonce bytes used to initialize MAC algorithm state

sinks.name: TEE_MACInit
sinks.reason: Determines how many bytes are read from the IV/nonce buffer

sinks.reason: provides bytes to be copied; may contain sensitive data

sinks.reason: controls how much attribute data is processed from the array, impacting parsing/copying

sinks.reason: supplies sensitive key material that is read/consumed to configure the cryptographic operation
